To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Na+/ Ca2+ exchange catalysed by heart mitochondria is inhibited by external Ca2+, that this inhibition is characterized by a half-saturation of 0.7 microM free Ca 2+, and that the inhibition is not due to competition with external Na+ or Sr2+ for substrate-binding sites.

the Na+/ Ca2+ carrier of the inner membrane of cardiac mitochondria has a regulatory site that binds extramitochondial Ca2+, and that the affinity for Ca2+ is high (Kd = 0.7 microM) and the binding is co-operative.
the Na+-induced release of Ca2+ from mitochondria is inhibited by external Ca2+.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of Ca2+ homeostasis in the cardiac cell by the Na+/ Ca2+ carrier of the mitochondria.
the regulation of mitochondrial Ca2+ transport and with the mechanism by which the Na+/Ca+ carrier is regulated.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms underlying the regulation of mitochondrial function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Na+/Sr2+ carrier contains at least two distinct classes of binding sites: one class, the substrate-binding sites, is responsible for cation translocation, and the other, the regulatory sites, is responsible, at least in part, for the sensitivity of Na+/Ca 2+ exchange to changes in extracellular [Ca 2+].
there is no evidence that the Na+/ Ca2+ carrier is directly involved in the Ca2+ signal transduction pathway of the cell.
the Na+/ Ca2+ carrier of heart mitochondria has at least two distinct classes of sites that interact with Ca2+.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Na+/H+ carrier is the major pathway for Ca2+ efflux from cardiac mitochondria at high [Ca2+] and that the Na+/ Ca2+ carrier is the main pathway for Ca2 efflux at low [Ca2+].
the carrier is regulated by both internal and external Ca2+.

the Na+/H+ antiporter of mitochondria is a carrier that contains at least three distinct types of sites: Na+ and Ca2+ translocation sites (i.e., substrate-binding sites); a regulatory site for Na+; and regulatory sites for Ca+.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Na+/ Ca2+ carrier of heart mitochondria contains regulatory sites that respond to changes in [Ca2+] in the physiological range.
the mitochondrial Na+/Ca2 + exchanger is regulated by extramitochon-drial Ca2+ and that this regulation may have physiological significance.
the mitochondrial Na+/Ca2+-carrier is a complex system, which is regulated by Ca2+ in several ways.
